scenes.title: 같은 회전을 다른 게임으로 옮겨 보기
lines: Alongside skiing, we compare aircraft and assembled components. Identify what changes and what remains the same.

scenes.title: 트레일메이커스: 기수와 날개를 따로 보기
lines: This is a Trailmakers aircraft. Inspect the red nose direction and blue wing direction together. After takeoff, the aircraft banks and later approaches level wings.
As with skiing, separate position from orientation: flight continues while orientation changes. These lines depict observed screen directions, not measured world angles or internal calculations.

scenes.title: 같은 각도, 다른 축
lines: For our defined aircraft model, x points forward, y points toward one wing, and z points up. This is not an assumed game coordinate system.

A ninety-degree turn around the forward axis leaves the nose direction unchanged and moves that wing direction upward. Its wxyz components are square root of two over two, the same value, zero, zero. The angle matches our earlier z-axis turn, but the axis occupies a different component.

scenes.title: 스페이스 엔지니어스: 부품 방향과 전체 자세 구분
lines: The component is turned sideways and upright. Inspect its other faces before calling the full orientation identical.

scenes.title: 되돌리는 것은 방향 연산입니다
lines: Standing upright alone does not establish an identical full orientation. We verify an exact inverse using the defined model. Define the initial model direction as one, zero, zero. A ninety-degree z-axis turn gives zero, one, zero; the opposite ninety-degree turn restores one, zero, zero.
The cancelling rotation is the inverse. It does not erase placement or traveled motion. These are defined, checkable model angles, not measurements from the footage.

scenes.title: 비시지: 선택한 부품에만 회전 적용
lines: Inspect the orange selected Besiege parts. A rotation changes their directions together while neighboring unselected parts remain.

scenes.title: 대상은 달라도 회전은 같은 규칙
lines: Applying the same ninety-degree model rotation to two perpendicular directions preserves their right angle. That differs from applying a different rotation to each direction.
Skis, aircraft, ship parts and assembled machines all present orientation problems despite their different shapes. We now return to the original calculation and apply the same rotation a second time.

scenes.title: 네 게임에서 입력과 결과 비교
lines: We again compare aircraft and assembled components. Connect the current direction, applied rotation and resulting direction across games.

scenes.title: 트레일메이커스: 물체의 방향과 보는 방향
lines: The Trailmakers aircraft banks and changes its nose direction. Follow the red nose line and blue wing line together to distinguish its orientation.
The camera also moves, so a screen tilt does not establish a ninety-degree world rotation. Our next model fixes the spatial axes and changes only the order of the rotations.

scenes.title: 같은 두 회전의 순서를 바꾸기
lines: Start with the upward model direction zero, zero, one. A ninety-degree fixed-world x turn followed by a ninety-degree fixed-world y turn gives zero, minus one, zero.

Reversing the order gives one, zero, zero. The individual turns match, but the final directions differ. This connects our verified right-handed convention and product order to an aircraft orientation problem.

scenes.title: 스페이스 엔지니어스: 현재 방향에서 목표 방향으로
lines: Standing the component upright requires a rotation between its current and target orientations.

scenes.title: 같은 축에서 목표까지 남은 회전
lines: In the defined same-axis model, the current z rotation is thirty degrees and the target is ninety; the remaining rotation is sixty, not an additional ninety.

Applying the world difference D to the current orientation A yields target B: D A equals B. Thus D equals B times the inverse of A. This same-axis check does not justify subtracting angles across different axes.

scenes.title: 비시지: 계산 결과가 부품의 방향을 바꿉니다
lines: The selected Besiege barrel directions change. Read a calculated direction-vector change on its attached object in the same way.

scenes.title: 벡터 계산을 보이는 결과로 읽기
lines: Turning the model direction one, zero, one by ninety degrees around z gives zero, one, one. Its horizontal component changes while its vertical component remains one.
Both lengths are square root of two: rotation changes direction and preserves length. This explains the preceding two-sided product, without inferring Besiege’s actual angles or implementation.
